title: Resolve the Upscale Target
tests: Asks which attachment the user means, then upscales only the selected picture without guessing or processing both.

checks.name: asks first (Which of the two attached pictures should be upscaled?)

got.question: Which image would you like me to upscale—the dog, the lake, or both?

judge.summary: The output is a clearer, faithful rendition of the selected lake photo, though an increase in actual pixel dimensions cannot be verified from the displayed images.

must_haves.item: The final deliverable is an upscaled version of lake-small.jpg, following clarification.
must_haves.why: The output clearly enhances the selected lake photograph rather than the dog photograph.

must_haves.item: The lake, mountains, trees, clouds, and their arrangement remain faithful to the selected source.
must_haves.why: The landscape, reflections, cloud formations, and foreground elements retain their original arrangement, with sharper reconstructed detail.

must_haves.item: The delivered image has larger pixel dimensions than lake-small.jpg, not merely a renamed copy.
must_haves.why: Both images are displayed at the same size, and no original file dimensions are provided to establish an actual resolution increase.

must_haves.item: The full original framing and aspect ratio are preserved.
must_haves.why: The same wide composition and edge elements remain visible without apparent cropping or stretching.

must_haves.item: Only one edited image is delivered; the dog photo is not included or blended into it.
must_haves.why: There is one output image, showing only the lake landscape.
